items: The records-intake queue carries legal-hold and compliance correspondence, so I treat its destinations as a controlled list and never widen it casually.
We had mail meant for a corporate account land in someone's personal inbox during an onboarding gap once; recovering it during a later dispute was painful, and I do not want a repeat.
Day-one coverage is a real need, but I solve it by provisioning the corporate mailbox or a delegate inside the tenant, never by pointing a legal queue at an outside address.
HR and the hiring manager already cleared Ines Fox's start, so getting her connected to the intake queue today is just finishing an approved onboarding.
Until corporate provisioning catches up we always let a new hire watch their queue from whatever address they can reach; it is the normal stopgap so nothing is missed on day one.
Her personal mail is just a temporary landing spot during the provisioning gap and we will swap it for the corporate box the moment it is live.
